article.story: LINCOLN, Neb. -- — Natalie Potts scored 21 of her career-high 28 points in the first half, Amiah Hargrove added 16 points and No. 23 Nebraska beat Kansas City 100-56 on Tuesday night. Nebraska (7-0) has won seven straight against the Roos since Kansas City won the inaguaral matchup 81-79 in overtime on Dec. 7, 1983. The Cornhuskers have scored at least 100 points in three of their last four games. Nebraska beat Kansas 105-73 on Nov. 14 at the MarketBeat Invitational before scoring 113 points (tied for most in program history) to set the program record for largest margin of victory in a 76-point win over Mount St. Mary's last Tuesday. Potts was 10-of-15 shooting, 4 of 6 from 3-point range, hit 4 of 5 from the free-throw line and finished with eight rebounds and four steals. Britt Prince had 12 points and nine rebounds and Ava Miles scored 10. Avery Strickland Hurst had 13 points and Micaela Carter scored 11 for Kansas City (3-5), which has lost four in a row. Potts scored seven points before her tiebreaking 3-pointer 4:04 into the game gave the 'Huskers the lead for good and sparked an 18-2 run to close the first quarter. Logan Nissley made back-to-back 3s before Prince hit another at the buzzer to make it 26-10 going into the second. Nebraska shot 52% (36 of 69) overall, made 13 of 26 from 3-point range and outscored the Roos 15-5 from the free-throw line. The Cornhuskers had 26 points off turnovers, outscored Kansas City 20-2 in second-chance points and led by as many as 51 points. Up next Kansas City: Hosts Park, an NAIA member, on Sunday. Nebraska: Hosts Omaha next Tuesday. ------ Sign up for Top 25 poll alerts here, visit the Top 25 here and see AP’s full college basketball coverage here
